correctness.rationale: Exact formulas for pair intersections derive from a factored conic difference; the two resulting quadratics split into two rational and two Q(sqrt13) points. Cyclic symmetry gives all twelve nodes. Smoothness determinant -256 and third-conic evaluations 2457 and norm -3^5*13 show all nodes ordinary and distinct at every p>=5 outside 7,13; direct special-prime substitution verifies both exceptions. Galois conjugations on these explicit nodes fix 12,6,4,2 points. Quadratic Frobenius and Chebotarev establish the prime counts/densities. Replayed standalone standard-library checker confirms coordinates/orbits and 20 independent Jacobian finite-field tests, not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Canonical three-conic arrangement from nodal-cubic osculation has a distinguished twelve-node zero-dimensional arithmetic scheme. Its minimal common field, Galois orbit partition, all prime-field rational point counts, and exactly two exceptional reductions are natural precise invariants, not arbitrary numerical slices. Geometric prior work fixes only complex incidence; arithmetic splitting and collision obstructions require the new computation. Useful in reduction, arithmetic incidence, and descent of explicit osculating configurations.
